blocks.text: For January 15 from SFO to Bangkok, the main schedule trade-off is arrival date versus a slightly shorter elapsed journey. The first option reaches Bangkok late on January 16, while the fastest reported direct-award schedule arrives the morning of January 17. Both are economy awards and leave SFO at 11:45 p.m. on January 15, so the later arrival is not a consequence of a later departure; it reflects the schedule and journey duration.

blocks.text: If minimizing time in transit matters more than arriving the previous evening, the next option is five minutes shorter overall and arrives at 9:50 a.m. on January 17. It does not buy a meaningfully earlier arrival than the first choice: that option gets you in on January 16 at 10:25 p.m. A separate-ticket business-class possibility also appears in the results, but it does not improve on the direct-award schedules’ arrival timing enough to make it the straightforward alternative; it adds a positioning flight and unresolved connection risk. An economy award is available on that same reported separate-ticket schedule, so the business cabin is not what creates a schedule advantage.
